sweep_summary: Polabian (pola1255) is in the catalog as weight-hedged (stress on the last non-reduced syllable: final if its vowel is full, else penult), deciding source Polański 2010, Gramatyka języka połabskiego, sec. 2.2.1 pp. 36-48 (rule p. 48). The stress-title sweep turned up a single bibliography item, Eisenberg 1991 'Syllabische Struktur und Wortakzent. Prinzipien der Prosodik deutscher Wörter' (Zeitschrift für Sprachwissenschaft 10(1): 37-64): it is about German word stress, and Glottolog's link to Polabian is a machine keyword assignment (record 411095 lgcode field: 'Polabian [pox] (computerized assignment from "wortakzent")', page saved). Relevance other-language-or-variety, priority none; the De Gruyter landing page and PDF link returned 405/empty to our fetchers (Crossref lists CC BY-NC-ND, so it may open in a browser), not pursued since it says nothing about Polabian; it should be dropped from the pola1255 bibliography. No new Polabian stress source was found; the best first-hand statement read in this sweep is Kortlandt's open 'Polabian accentuation' (already on file from the 2026-09-16 audit pass), p. 1: 'The stress fell on the last full vowel of a word form, which was found either in the final or in the penultimate syllable. In the latter instance, the final syllable contained a reduced vowel', which confirms the catalog coding and does not supersede Polański 2010. Files and the fetch log are in .

new_statements.quote: From a synchronic point of view, the accentuation of Late Polabian has been clarified by Trubetzkoy (1929) and Olesch (1973, 1974). The stress fell on the last full vowel of a word form, which was found either in the final or in the penulti-mate syllable. In the latter instance, the final syllable contained a reduced vowel. This rule was challenged by Kuryłowicz (1955), who maintained that the stress was fixed on the initial syllable of the word. [...] I therefore think that it is correct for an earlier stage of the language, which may conveniently be called Middle Polabian.

new_statements.reading: Late Polabian stress is right-edge and conditioned by vowel quality: it falls on the final syllable when that syllable's vowel is full, otherwise on the penult (the final then having a reduced vowel), i.e. on the last full (non-reduced) vowel of the word form. Kuryłowicz's fixed-initial stress is accepted only for an earlier 'Middle Polabian' stage. This is the same rule as the catalog's deciding source, Polański 2010 p. 48 ('miejscem akcentu połabskiego była ostatnia niezredukowana sylaba wyrazu' = the place of Polabian stress was the last non-reduced syllable of the word; re-verified in the held extracted text at, folio 'GP.indb 47'/p. 48), and it confirms the weight-hedged coding (weight = full vs reduced vowel). Note: this file was already fetched sources and logged as 'confirms' by the 2026-09-16 audit pass (out/store/A/ fetched_now); it was re-read, not newly acquired, in this sweep.

audit.reasoning: The classification (weight-hedged, right edge, weight = full vs reduced vowel: stress on the final syllable if its vowel is full, else the penult) rests on the standard modern reference grammar of Polabian by the field's leading specialist, held locally as the library's open PDF, and every quoted fragment was found verbatim at the cited pages (38, 40, 45, 47-48, rule on p.48). Polabian is extinct since the 18th century, so no instrumental study can supersede a philological reconstruction; Polański 2010 is the latest and fullest such reconstruction and reviews all rivals.
